meta.tagline: Knights' walls, three hundred days of sun, and an island where two seas meet

overview.title: Welcome to Rhodes
overview.intro: As the ferry nears Mandraki harbour, the walls salute you from the Middle Ages: Rhodes is a Mediterranean island holding one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities. Inside the walls, knights' lanes; outside, palm-lined Italian boulevards; and to the south stretches an island of wind and sea. An hour from the Turkish coast lies another world — though don't be surprised when the tea and the conversation feel familiar.

local_word.definition: Greek for 'love of the stranger': hospitality's ancient name. The free dessert at the table, the shopkeeper walking you to your turn, the pension owner saying 'sit, have a coffee' — all daily forms of filoxenia.

rules.title: Live the Old Town at morning or evening
rules.description: By midday the walled city surrenders to cruise crowds. Before 9 am and after 6 pm the lanes belong to locals and to you; the stone glows differently in evening light.

rules.title: Don't plan the island from one point
rules.description: Rhodes is big: Lindos is 55 km away, Prasonisi 90 km south. Rent a car or plan around the bus timetable; the 'everything is close' illusion ends the day on the road.

rules.title: Sort the ferry paperwork early
rules.description: On the Marmaris and Fethiye lines, book ahead and arrive early for passport control; confirm your return sailing on day one. The summer wind (meltemi) sometimes rewrites the schedule.

tip.label: The Rhodes philosophy
tip.text: Rhodes is two islands: the north's motion and the south's solitude. Don't leave without both — the day that starts in a knights' lane and ends in a southern cove is the day you understand the island.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: At the northern tip everything is close; for the rest of the island you need wheels or patience.

items.title: Ferries — Marmaris and the islands
items.description: About an hour from Marmaris by catamaran, daily in summer. Big ferries from Piraeus, and day boats to the neighbouring islands (Symi, Halki) leave from Mandraki.

items.title: KTEL buses — two coasts
items.description: The east line (toward Lindos) and the west line leave from separate terminals; Lindos runs frequently. Cheap and air-conditioned — but always check the last return.

items.title: Rental car — the key to the south
items.description: The only real option for Prasonisi, Monolithos and the west coast. Roads are good, traffic calm; petrol stations thin out in the south. Book ahead in summer.

items.title: Scooters and ATVs
items.description: Practical around town; but the meltemi blows seriously on the west side. Car for the long hauls, scooter for short scouting — that's the right formula.

items.title: Taxis
items.description: Short city rides are reasonable; for long routes like Lindos, fix the price before boarding. The airport-city fare list hangs at the rank.

callout.label: Symi tip
callout.text: Give one day to Symi: 50 minutes by morning boat from Mandraki, and a pastel neoclassical amphitheatre of a harbour awaits. That's where the Symi shrimp is eaten — and the return boat is never missed.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: Inside the walls amid history, in a beach town, or in the empty south — on Rhodes all three are possible.

local_word.definition: The castle: the walled old quarter of a Greek island. Thousands still live inside Rhodes's kastro — your hotel's stone wall may be six hundred years old.

items.name: Old Town (inside the walls)
items.description: Stone-mansion guesthouses inside the medieval lanes: the city is yours before the crowds arrive, and at night the lantern-lit streets are a film set. Car access is limited — luggage gets walked — but it's worth it.

items.name: New Town / Mandraki
items.description: Harbour, market, cafés and the town beach within walking distance; the ideal base if you arrive by ferry. The Italian-era architecture and the evening promenade are a surprise pleasure.

items.name: Lindos
items.description: A whitewashed village under an acropolis, with two bays: Rhodes's most famous view. Very crowded on summer days, but the village calms at dusk; for honeymooners and view-chasers.

items.name: Ialysos / Ixia — the windward side
items.description: The west coast's breezy beaches are among Europe's favourite windsurf and kite spots; hotels are large, sunsets long. For those who like their sea with waves.

items.name: The south — toward Gennadi/Monolithos
items.description: Where the crowds end: empty beaches, village tavernas and a starry sky. A car is essential; the reward is the island at its purest.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Rhodes is the island of the sun; the question is never 'will it shine' but 'how many others will be there'.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Green Rhodes
items.subtitle: Spring · Flowering walls, the sea warming up
items.description: The island at its greenest, the Valley of the Butterflies still calm, the Old Town at strolling temperature. In June the sea warms while the crowds stay below July levels.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May you can climb the Lindos acropolis even at noon; in July the same stairway is an oven. Value the early season.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Full Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Heat, wind and full beaches
items.description: The eastern bays lie warm and still, the west side cools in the meltemi; nightlife and boat trips peak. On cruise days the Old Town overflows at noon — the morning/evening rule saves lives.

callout.label: Heat warning
callout.text: The Lindos acropolis and Filerimos are shadeless at midday; don't climb without water, a hat and a morning hour.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Golden Sea
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, calm streets
items.description: September and October are the island's crown: the sea like a bath, the crowds receded, the prices down. Even in November, sunny lunches happen by the water.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October the southern beaches (Gennadi, Prasonisi) are nearly private; take the car and go cove by cove.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Locals' Island
items.subtitle: Winter · Silent walls, open cafés
items.description: Tourist facilities partly close but the city keeps living; you walk the Old Town nearly alone. Walking weather between rain breaks — and the year's most honest prices.

callout.label: Winter tip
callout.text: Walking the Street of the Knights alone in winter is a Rhodes summer never shows; the museums stay open, the coffee stays hot.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Rhodes kitchen is island Greece at its heartiest: fried meze, fresh fish and wine down from the mountain villages.

local_word.definition: The house of ouzo and meze: small plates line up on the table and the hours pass by themselves. Find a good ouzeri on Rhodes and cancel your other plans for the evening.

items.name: Pitaroudia — chickpea fritters
items.description: Rhodes's signature meze: chickpeas kneaded with tomato and mint, then fried; crisp outside, soft within. One of ouzo's best friends.

items.name: The day's fish — grilled
items.description: Bream, red mullet or whatever the meltemi brought: char-grilled, with lemon, by the water. Choosing your fish from the display by weight is normal here.

items.name: Symi shrimp
items.description: The neighbouring island's tiny shrimp are fried whole and eaten shell and all: crisp, salty, addictive. Found in Rhodes tavernas too — ask for today's.
items.tag: Eat with the shell · Symi style

items.name: Oven lamb of the mountain villages
items.description: The plate of the highlands (toward Embonas): lamb or goat, hours in the oven, island pasta alongside. The feast of Sunday afternoons.

items.name: The wines of Embonas
items.description: Embonas, the vineyard village under Mount Attavyros, is the island's wine capital: Athiri whites and Amorgiano reds. Village winery tastings are warm and generous.

items.name: Melekouni and talagoutes
items.description: The sesame-honey wedding sweet melekouni and honey-drizzled village pancakes talagoutes: the island's sweet memory. Fresh at markets and village festivals.

callout.label: The taverna rule
callout.text: In the Old Town, avoid the 'doorway hawker + multilingual photo menu' pairing; one lane back, the place chalking its menu feeds you twice as well for the same money.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Rhodes's celebrities live on postcards; these six are the reward of whoever takes the car keys.

items.rarity: A castle on the cliff's edge
items.name: Monolithos Castle
items.description: A knights' castle set atop a 236-metre rock on the west coast: a few walls, a chapel and an endless sea. At sunset, the island's most dramatic stage.

items.name: Prasonisi
items.description: At the island's southern tip, the two sides of a sand spit: one sea calm, the other the wind's. Mecca for kitesurfers; even watching is a show.

items.name: Seven Springs (Epta Piges)
items.description: Streams, peacocks and a dark water tunnel inside a pine forest: walking the tunnel out to the lake is the island's classic dare.

items.name: Kritinia Castle
items.description: A ruined knights' castle looking over the west coast and Halki island: free entry, no crowds, a free sunset. A village taverna nearby is the bonus.

items.name: Anthony Quinn Bay
items.description: The turquoise cove named after 'The Guns of Navarone': a snorkelling paradise among the rocks. Go early — the boats arrive at noon.

items.name: Filerimos and the Golgotha way
items.description: Above ancient Ialysos: a monastery, a cypress-lined 'Golgotha' walk and a giant cross; peacocks accompany you, and both coasts show below.

callout.label: Southern tip
callout.text: On your day south, take lunch at a village taverna in Gennadi or Lachania; the menu is short, the fish fresh, the bill half.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Rhodes is an honest island; the traps are squeezed along the cruise route. Know these four — the rest is filoxenia.

items.name: The hawkered tourist menu inside the walls
items.description: Around Socratous Street, the places calling you in with photo menus sell frozen moussaka at castle prices.
items.instead: Go a lane or two deeper, or step outside the walls: at chalk-menu ouzeris the same money buys the real thing.

items.name: Mistaking Faliraki for the whole island
items.description: The party beach's bars and jet-ski noise are not Rhodes's shop window; ending the island there leaves it half-seen.
items.instead: Give a day to the south: Gennadi's emptiness, Prasonisi's wind, Monolithos's cliff — the island's true face is there.

items.name: Renting an uninsured ATV
items.description: The cheap-looking quads are dangerous on windy roads and ruinous in a scrape; licence and insurance checks get skipped.
items.instead: Rent a car or a fully insured scooter; never sign without reading the damage excess.

items.name: Haggling an 'all-inclusive boat tour' at the harbour
items.description: Some tours charge on board for what was 'included', and on a packed deck the cove loses its charm.
items.instead: Ask in writing what's included (food, drinks, stops); the scheduled boats to Symi or Halki are usually the better deal.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: When a cruise ship is in port, leave the Old Town for the south or the beach; when it sails at dusk, the walls are yours again.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Knights + Lindos: the island's two summits

steps.title: Old Town — before the crowds
steps.description: Walk the Street of the Knights to the Palace of the Grand Master; the stone is cool, the lanes empty.

steps.title: Palace and walls
steps.description: The palace courtyard and mosaics, then the wall walk (on open days): tiled roofs and two harbours from above.

steps.title: Road to Lindos
steps.description: 50 minutes by bus or car; a quick look at the Kallithea thermal cove on the way is allowed.

steps.title: Lindos lunch + acropolis
steps.description: A light lunch in the village, then the climb: St Paul's Bay through the columns — the island's most famous frame.

steps.title: Sea break
steps.description: Swim at Lindos main beach or St Paul's Bay; the afternoon light turns the bay deep green.

steps.title: Mandraki evening
steps.description: Back in town, walk the promenade between the deer statues; open dinner at an ouzeri with pitaroudia.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the island as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Knights and Lindos
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Old Town, palace, Lindos, Mandraki.

steps.title: Symi escape
steps.description: Morning boat to Symi: the pastel harbour, Panormitis Monastery, Symi shrimp at noon; back for a night walk in the Old Town — walls under lanterns.

steps.title: The wild west and south
steps.description: By car down the west coast: Filerimos, Kritinia Castle, a wine-tasting lunch in Embonas, the Monolithos sunset; one last swim in a southern cove on the way home.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Three words of Greek open the doors; arriving from the neighbouring shore guarantees a smile on top.

items.meaning: Hello / goodbye — the formal, safe greeting
Thank you — looks hard, lands by the second try
Please / you're welcome — Greek's joker card
Cheers! — ouzo glasses rise to this
Good morning — the word that lights up faces at the morning market
